stories.summary: Singapore has grown 28% bigger since independence through land reclamation, and the government has announced ambitious plans for more reclamation along the southern coast. A new generation is now questioning the cost, with rare public resistance to clearing forests for development. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong set out his vision for the country's future in his August National Day Rally speech.
stories.title: Singapore's Endless Hunt for Space Faces Rare Public Resistance
stories.why: Land is Singapore's scarcest resource — the pushback marks a shift in how the growth-versus-green trade-off is debated.

stories.summary: Singapore's top law firm was fined S$247,000 by the Personal Data Protection Commission over a 2023 breach in which personal data of more than 100,000 people — including NRIC numbers, addresses, bank account details and insurance information — was stolen. The breach was discovered on 27 July 2023 after the firm's cybersecurity manager mistook vendor alerts for planned testing. The fine was cut from S$317,000 after the PDPC accepted some of the firm's representations.
stories.title: Rajah & Tann fined S$247,000 after personal data of over 100,000 people was stolen
stories.why: A basic failure to act on security alerts at one of Singapore's largest firms — a warning for every organisation holding personal data.

stories.summary: Singaporean trainee doctor Ryan Cho, 29, was remanded in custody in Melbourne on 26 November after a three-day pre-sentence hearing over secretly filming 874 victims across three Melbourne hospitals and shared homes in 2024–2025. He had pleaded guilty to 13 charges, including producing intimate images, stalking and possessing child abuse material. He is due to be sentenced on 12 February 2027.
stories.title: Singaporean doctor who secretly filmed hundreds of women remanded ahead of sentencing
stories.why: One of Australia's largest voyeurism prosecutions — and a case that has left victims with lasting trauma and raised questions about hospital safeguards.

stories.summary: SAP is preparing to cut at least 10,000 positions — about 9% of its global workforce — as chief executive Christian Klein reshapes the software giant around an AI-first strategy, Bloomberg reported. Product, engineering and sales are in focus, and the final number could change after labour negotiations. It would be SAP's second restructuring of about 10,000 roles in under three years.
stories.title: SAP weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI restructuring
stories.why: Europe's most valuable tech company is the latest to trade headcount for AI — a sign of how the AI buildout is reshaping even the software giants.

stories.summary: Japan is drafting an amendment to its AI Promotion Act that would impose binding duties on providers of the most powerful 'frontier AI' systems — requiring them to report accidents and vulnerabilities, refuse queries about cyberattack methods and hazardous substances, and verify the identities of users of cyberattack-capable models. Enforcement would follow a three-step ladder: recommendation, formal order, then penalty. The rules would cover foreign providers with a large Japanese user base, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Alibaba and DeepSeek. The government aims to present the outline to its expert panel by year-end and submit a bill in next year's Diet session.
stories.title: Japan moves to give its AI rules real teeth
stories.why: Japan would join the EU in moving from voluntary AI guidelines to enforceable duties — and, unlike the US, it would bind foreign labs directly.

stories.summary: Stocks rose in Europe and Asia as buyers returned to technology shares after days of sharp swings. Europe's Stoxx 600 rallied 1.7% and a gauge of Asian stocks climbed 0.8%, only its second advance in 11 sessions. Memory giants SK Hynix and Kioxia outperformed in Asia, and Taiwan and South Korea's tech benchmarks rose more than 2%. The gains followed Wednesday's late-session dip-buying on Wall Street that pulled the Nasdaq 100 back from bear-market territory ahead of Thanksgiving. Brent crude topped US$96 a barrel for the first time in more than a week.
stories.title: Global stocks climb as AI trade mounts a comeback
stories.why: The AI trade is showing signs of life after a bruising November — but strategists warn Friday will be the real test of whether the rebound holds.

stories.summary: Asian stocks were poised to extend their rebound as buyers returned to the AI trade, with futures for Japan and South Korea pointing higher and Australian shares opening up. Oil climbed after Yemen's Houthi rebels struck a key Saudi refinery, with Brent rising more than 2% to above US$96 a barrel for a third straight session. Bitcoin traded around US$60,400 and gold held near US$3,565 an ounce. US markets reopen on Friday for a shortened session after Thanksgiving.
stories.title: Asian stock futures signal gains, oil advances
stories.why: The rebound is fragile — traders see few catalysts to sustain it and are looking to next month's Federal Reserve meeting for direction on borrowing costs.

stories.summary: Core consumer prices in Tokyo rose 2.9% in November from a year earlier, government data showed on Friday — up from 2.6% in October but below the 3.0% forecast. Headline CPI held at 2.8%, while the core-core index excluding fresh food and energy eased to 2.5%. The figures, a leading indicator for nationwide inflation, will feed into the Bank of Japan's policy meeting ending 18 December, with markets pricing a high chance of a rate rise.
stories.title: Tokyo core CPI rises 2.9% in November, strengthening case for BOJ hike
stories.why: Persistent inflation above the BOJ's 2% target keeps a December hike firmly on the table, with the yen near 159 to the dollar.

stories.summary: Two Italian technicians working for Rheinmetall Italia were killed in a drone attack in Kuwait on Thursday that Italy and Kuwait blamed on Iran, though Tehran denied any involvement. The two were at an air defence surveillance station when it was targeted by Iranian drones; a Pakistani national and a Kuwaiti army captain were also injured. Italy said it would lodge a complaint with the Iranian embassy. The attack comes as Iran has stepped up strikes on Gulf states hosting US military bases since the US-Israeli attacks on Iran in February.
stories.title: Two Italians killed in attack on Kuwait site, Iran denies involvement
stories.why: The first fatal strike in Kuwait for months shows the Iran conflict widening to Gulf states caught between the US and Tehran.

stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Ukrainians to heed air-raid sirens in the coming days, saying Russia is completing preparations for another massive strike on energy infrastructure, logistics and essential services. It was his second such warning this week. The warning followed an overnight barrage of ballistic missiles and 113 drones that hit 20 locations, including a Kyiv shopping mall, injuring seven. Ukraine hit back at a Russian refinery, a Transneft oil facility and the Marinovka airfield.
stories.title: Zelensky warns Russia preparing massive strike on Ukraine's power grid as winter nears
stories.why: Russia is trying to leave Ukrainians without electricity, heating and running water as winter sets in — and Kyiv is short of the Patriot interceptors needed to stop ballistic missiles.

stories.summary: India and the UAE have agreed to accelerate joint development and production of next-generation defence equipment, the Indian Defence Ministry said. The deal was reached at the 14th India-UAE Joint Defence Cooperation Committee meeting in Abu Dhabi, co-chaired by Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and UAE Under Secretary Lt Gen Ibrahim Nasser M Al Alawi. The two sides also agreed to expand cooperation in defence technology, AI, cyber security, military training and maritime safety.
stories.title: India, UAE agree to speed up joint development of defence equipment
stories.why: The partnership links India's manufacturing scale with Gulf funding and reach — a new axis in defence-industrial cooperation.

stories.summary: The 12th India-Sri Lanka joint military exercise, Mitra Shakti-XII, concluded at Maduru Oya in Sri Lanka with a final demonstration at the Army Training School. The two-week exercise, from 13 to 26 November, involved a 170-member Indian contingent training alongside Sri Lankan troops in counter-terrorism operations in a semi-urban environment under a UN mandate.
stories.title: India-Sri Lanka joint military exercise Mitra Shakti XII concludes
stories.why: The annual exercise is the clearest signal of the two neighbours' steady military engagement — and of India's role as Sri Lanka's main security partner.

stories.summary: CNA Verify found at least 188 Threads accounts posing as Johor residents, posting coordinated complaints about fictional firms — 'Snoring Doughnut Dragon', 'Cosmic Custard Chicken', 'Floating Sausage Library' — supposedly mismanaging multi-million-ringgit projects. The accounts posted in bursts (92 posts in 11 hours on 13 November), shared identical wording, and mostly had no followers and a single post; 135 joined Threads only in November. Threads' own labels put 93 of the accounts in Pakistan and 36 in Russia. Johor's chief minister posted about the accounts on 16 November, and a police report was made. Experts say the operation may be a 'test run' by an influence-for-hire vendor.
stories.title: 'Snoring Doughnut Dragon': Nearly 200 Threads accounts posed as Johor residents to complain about fake firms
stories.why: A textbook influence operation on Singapore's doorstep — fake grassroots complaints designed to look like genuine residents pressing a chief minister, with unclear backing and a possible commercial motive.

tldr: Bloomberg reports Singapore's new land-reclamation and forest-clearing plans are drawing rare public resistance.
SAP weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs — 9% of staff — in an AI-driven restructuring.
Global stocks climb as the AI trade mounts a comeback after Wall Street's late rebound.
Two Italians killed in an Iranian drone attack on a Kuwait air-defence site.
CNA Verify exposes ~200 coordinated Threads accounts posing as Johor residents to push fake complaints.
